Havana, Cuba · [maicel.monzon@gmail.com](mailto:maicel.monzon@gmail.com) · [bioestadisticaedu.com](https://bioestadisticaedu.com) · [github.com/maicel1978](https://github.com/maicel1978) · ORCID [0000-0003-2117-9145](https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2117-9145)

## Profile

Medical doctor and biostatistician (second-degree specialist, PhD in Medical Sciences) with 20 years of experience turning complex health data into decision-ready evidence. Recent work for WFP: analysis of a national household income and expenditure survey to estimate apparent micronutrient intake and model large-scale food fortification scenarios, delivered as a reproducible R pipeline and an e-learning platform. Background in clinical trial statistics and regulatory review. Remote or field-based; Spanish (native) and English.

## Core skills

- **Household surveys and nutrition:** HCES analysis, apparent intake, adult male equivalents, food composition crosswalks, EAR cut-point and probability approaches, fortification scenario modelling.
- **Statistics:** design-based inference for complex samples, clinical prediction models, sample size and randomisation, statistical analysis plans for clinical trials.
- **Reproducible workflows:** R (survey, srvyr, tidyverse), Quarto, Git/GitHub, audit trails with control figures; Python.
- **Capacity strengthening:** curriculum design, e-learning modules, training of health professionals.

## Experience

**Consultant, Programme Policy (Nutrition)** — World Food Programme, Dominican Republic Country Office · Jul–Oct 2026

- Resolved the open question of whether the 2018 National Household Income and Expenditure Survey (ENGIH) could support nutrition analysis: delivered the feasibility report early and extended it to an advanced micronutrient intake analysis.
- Built a reproducible R pipeline (survey design, paired differences between scenarios with confidence intervals) estimating the potential contribution of current national standards, WHO-recommended levels and rice fortification to iron, folate, zinc and vitamin A adequacy.
- Identified that one survey section records weights rather than consumed quantities, preventing a biased intake estimate.
- Designed and deployed an e-learning platform on coverage, consumption and contribution of fortified foods, with modular R code, scripts and question banks ([fortificacion.netlify.app](https://fortificacion.netlify.app)).
- Presented results to WFP teams and partner organisations. Manuscript for a peer-reviewed journal in preparation with WFP co-authors.

**Clinical Trials Reviewer** — Centre for State Control of Medicines, Equipment and Medical Devices (CECMED), Havana · 2023–present

- Review of clinical trial protocols and results for regulatory decision-making.

**Assistant Professor of Biostatistics** — National School of Public Health (ENSAP), Havana · 2022–present

- Teaching of statistical methods for public health and of clinical trial design and conduct at postgraduate level.

**Biostatistician; Head of Statistical Analysis (from 2019)** — National Coordinating Centre for Clinical Trials (CENCEC), Havana · 2013–2022

- Statistical analysis plans, sample size calculation, randomisation and final analyses for efficacy and safety trials of medicines and biotechnology products.

**Statistician and Head of Research** — Dr. José Gregorio Hernández Mission, Venezuela · 2010–2013

- Statistician of the national Comprehensive Study of Persons with Disabilities; led the design and conduct of research at the National Centre of Medical Genetics.

**Bioinformatician and Lecturer** — Centre for Cybernetics Applied to Medicine (CECAM), Havana · 2004–2010

- Predictive and mathematical models for epidemiological analysis; teaching of artificial intelligence applied to health sciences.
